keys.usage: Sign ThoughtProof validation artifacts and Sentinel L1 verdict attestations (pilot)

canonicalization.note: Always prefer verifying Ed25519 over the exact UTF-8 bytes in attestation.canonicalJson (or equivalent issued field). Profile names below describe how those bytes were produced — do not re-canonicalize from a pretty-printed object unless you implement the named profile bit-exactly.

rfc8785-canonicalize-utf8-v1.name: rfc8785-canonicalize-utf8-v1
steps: Serialize with canonicalize(body) → UTF-8 string (no pretty print)
Sign those exact bytes with Ed25519 (pure, no prehash context)
canonicalHash = 0x || sha256(those same bytes) as hex
Third party: verify signature over attestation.canonicalJson as issued

tp-json-sort-keys-recursive-utf8-v1.name: tp-json-sort-keys-recursive-utf8-v1
tp-json-sort-keys-recursive-utf8-v1.implementation: recursive key sort + JSON.stringify (no extra whitespace)
steps: Remove top-level fields: signature, artifactHash, signed
Recursively sort all object keys (arrays keep order)
Serialize with JSON.stringify (no extra whitespace; UTF-8)
Sign those exact bytes with Ed25519 (pure, no prehash context)
artifactHash = 0x || sha256(those same bytes) as hex

notes: Pilot key — not HSM-backed. Rotate via new keyId + status=retired on old keys.
HMAC shared-secret signing is not used for public artifacts.
Two canonicalization profiles exist on purpose (L1 verdict vs older validation artifacts). Do not mix names.
Stephen/third-party path for L1: GET well-known → Ed25519 verify(signature, attestation.canonicalJson).
